subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

options: The detailed examination of an existing product to learn how it functions and how it was made
The process of advertising a finished product to potential customers
The stage of packaging a product ready for sale
The method of pricing a product for the market
questions.explain: Product analysis is the systematic study of an existing product to understand its function, materials and manufacture.

questions.q: In product analysis, the term 'aesthetics' refers to:
options: How a product appeals to the senses, especially its visual appearance
How much a product costs to manufacture
How strong the joints in a product are
How the product is transported to shops
questions.explain: Aesthetics concerns how attractive a product is to the senses, such as its shape, colour and texture.

questions.q: Why do designers carry out disassembly (taking a product apart) when analysing it?
options: To understand how the components fit together and how the product was manufactured
To increase the selling price of the product
To make the product heavier and more durable
To remove any branding before selling it again
questions.explain: Disassembly reveals internal construction, component choices and manufacturing methods that are hidden from the outside.

options: The collection and use of human body measurement data
The study of how machines are powered
The testing of a material's electrical resistance
The costing of materials used in a product
questions.explain: Anthropometrics is the gathering of body measurements so products can be designed to fit users.

questions.q: Ergonomics in product design is mainly concerned with:
options: How well a product fits and can be comfortably used by people
How cheaply a product can be mass produced
How a product is recycled at the end of its life
How a product is protected by a patent
questions.explain: Ergonomics ensures a product is comfortable, safe and efficient for people to use.

questions.q: When using anthropometric data, designers usually design to accommodate which range of users?
options: The 5th to 95th percentile
Only the 50th percentile
Only the 100th percentile
The 25th to 75th percentile
questions.explain: Designing for the 5th to 95th percentile accommodates the great majority of the population.

questions.q: A designer wants to check whether a new kettle handle is comfortable for a wide range of people. Which approach is most appropriate?
options: Carry out user trials with people of different hand sizes
Measure only the designer's own hand
Choose the cheapest handle available
Test only the colour of the handle
questions.explain: User trials with a range of people gather ergonomic evidence about comfort for different users.

questions.q: The 'function' of a product refers to:
options: The job or purpose the product is designed to perform
The colour scheme chosen for the product
The name of the company that made it
The shop where it is sold
questions.explain: Function is what a product is meant to do, its intended job or purpose.

questions.q: In product analysis, 'form' most closely means:
options: The shape, size and overall appearance of a product
The electrical power a product uses
The weight of the packaging
The warranty offered with a product
questions.explain: Form describes the physical shape, size and appearance of a product.

questions.q: The design principle 'form follows function' means that:
options: The appearance of a product should be shaped mainly by its intended purpose
A product should always be as decorative as possible
The cheapest material should always be used
The product should be as large as possible
questions.explain: 'Form follows function' means a product's shape should be led by what it needs to do.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes a key property of thermoplastics?
options: They can be reheated and reshaped many times
They set permanently and cannot be remelted
They are always electrical conductors
They cannot be moulded at all
questions.explain: Thermoplastics soften when heated and can be reshaped repeatedly, unlike thermosetting plastics.

questions.q: Why might a designer choose acrylic for a clear light cover?
options: It is transparent, weather resistant and can be easily shaped when heated
It rusts quickly and is very heavy
It conducts electricity well
It rots when exposed to light
questions.explain: Acrylic is a transparent thermoplastic that is durable and easily formed, making it suitable for covers.

questions.q: A designer needs a material for an outdoor bench frame that is lightweight, strong and resistant to corrosion. Which material is most suitable?
options: Aluminium
Mild steel
Cast iron
MDF
questions.explain: Aluminium is light, strong and naturally corrosion resistant, ideal for outdoor use.

questions.q: A product feels comfortable and safe to hold, its buttons are easy to reach, and it works well for its task. This shows good consideration of:
options: Function and ergonomics
Packaging colour only
Advertising strategy
Shop location
questions.explain: Ease of use, comfort and effective performance reflect good ergonomic and functional design.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correct list of the '6 Rs' of sustainable design?
options: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Refuse, Rethink, Repair
Reduce, Repaint, Reheat, Resell, Rebrand, Reboot
Recycle, Return, Refund, Reserve, Repeat, Remove
Reuse, Redraw, Restart, Reorder, Reply, Report
questions.explain: The 6 Rs are Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Refuse, Rethink and Repair.

options: Processing used materials so they can be made into new products
Throwing waste materials into landfill
Burning waste to remove it completely
Storing products unused in a warehouse
questions.explain: Recycling reprocesses used materials into new products, reducing waste and raw material use.

questions.q: In the 6 Rs, the aim of 'Reduce' is to:
options: Use fewer materials and less energy when making and using a product
Make products as large as possible
Increase the amount of packaging used
Repair products only after they break
questions.explain: 'Reduce' means minimising the materials and energy needed, lowering environmental impact.

questions.q: A company redesigns its packaging so it uses much less card while still protecting the product. Which of the 6 Rs does this best represent?
options: Reduce
Refuse
Rethink
Recycle
questions.explain: Using less material to do the same job is an example of Reduce.

questions.q: A designer ensures that worn parts of a product can be replaced rather than throwing the whole item away. Which of the 6 Rs does this show?
options: Repair
Refuse
Rethink
Reduce
questions.explain: Designing so parts can be replaced extends a product's life through Repair.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Design & Technology (0445) syllabus; Product Analysis
